'''Thomas Edward Forster''' (born 12 April 1948) is a British [[Set theory|set theorist]] and philosopher. His work has focused on [[Willard Van Orman Quine|Quine]]'s [[New Foundations]], the theory of [[Well-quasi-ordering|well-quasi-orders]] and [[Better-quasi-ordering|better-quasi-orders]], and various topics in philosophy.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Forster|first=Thomas|date=|title=CV|url=https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/~tf/tfbib2.pdf|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>

==Career==
Forster completed a PhD at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1977, with the dissertation ''NF'' on [[New Foundations]], jointly supervised by [[Adrian Mathias]] and Maurice Boffa.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|77585}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis|title=NF|first=T. E.|last=Forster|year=1977|publisher=University of Cambridge|doi=10.17863/CAM.16205|hdl=1810/223940}}</ref>

Forster is an Affiliated Lecturer at [[Faculty of Mathematics, University of Cambridge|DPMMS]], Cambridge,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr Thomas Forster {{!}} Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics|url=https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/person/tef10|access-date=2020-11-29|website=www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk}}</ref> a [[Bye-Fellow|bye-fellow]] at [[Queens' College, Cambridge|Queens' College]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr Thomas Forster {{!}} Queens' College|url=https://www.queens.cam.ac.uk/dr-thomas-forster|access-date=2020-11-29|website=www.queens.cam.ac.uk}}</ref> and holds honorary appointments for many other organisations worldwide, including the [[Center for Philosophy of Science]] in Pittsburgh, the Centre National de Recherches de Logique in Belgium, and the Centre for Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science at the [[University of Auckland]].<ref name=":0" /> Amongst his undergraduate supervisees are [[Phebe Mann]], [[Rosi Sexton]], [[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Richard Taylor]], [[Rebecca Kitteridge]], [[Doug Gurr]], [[Sarah Flannery]] and [[Ursula Martin]].

==Recognition==
Forster was awarded the [[Smith's Prize|J.T. Knight Prize]] as a PhD student at [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]] in 1974.<ref name=":0" /> His article "The Iterative Conception of Set"<ref>{{Cite journal|last=FORSTER|first=THOMAS|title=The Iterative Conception of Set|date=June 2008|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1017/s1755020308080064|journal=The Review of Symbolic Logic|volume=1|issue=1|pages=97–110|doi=10.1017/s1755020308080064|s2cid=15231169 |issn=1755-0203|citeseerx=10.1.1.157.5010}}</ref> was recognised by the [[Philosopher's Annual|Philosophers' Annual]] as one of the ten best philosophy articles of 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Philosopher's Annual|url=https://www.pgrim.org/philosophersannual/past.html|access-date=2020-11-29|website=www.pgrim.org}}</ref>
